newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia breaks up sophisticated counterfeit ring.
newsitem.headline: Colombia breaks up sophisticated counterfeit ring.

text.p: Police broke up a sophisticated counterfeit ring operating out of southwest Colombia on Thursday that had produced millions in bogus U.S. currency.
Col. Benigno Esteban Pineros, National Police commander in Cali, said a dozen people were arrested in a total of 14 raids there and in the nearby towns of Buga and Tulua.
High-tech photo-composition equipment, a lithograph and more than 1,000 negatives used to print dollars were seized in the raids, he said.

The paper used to print the illegal tender was the same as Venezuela's central bank uses to print its bolivar currency but it underwent a "special laundering process" before being coverted into dollars, Pineros said.
He said $1 million worth of phony dollars was seized in the raids and that police had confiscated another $5 million still in the process of being counterfeited.
